title: How much better does MZ run compared to MV?

posts.author: PuppetWraith
posts.body:
Sorry if this is a dumb question, but I guess I'm just having trouble deciding between which engine to choose. I've been using VX Ace for the longest time, and MV seems better in almost every way for what I want to do with it, but I've heard MZ runs way better than MV, but idk how true that is, and I've been having a hard time finding details. Does the game itself run better? Or just the engine? Idk I guess I feel like MV will be better for what I want, but I have doubts about performance.
Thank you for your time/adivce!

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body: Generally MV users will update the nw.js version to improve performance. I don't know if anyone stress tested MV + updated nw.js vs MZ to compare.

posts.author: Rifleman_XM8
posts.body:
In general, there isn't much difference between MV and MZ; they share resources such as audio files, characters, and tilesets. Except for plugins, which require separate use.
I recommend MZ because it offers greater flexibility in use.
Recommended to buy during a Steam sale for significantly lower prices.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
completely aside from the performance, MZ is additionally the more modern version that has a lot of features added compared to MV, like particle animations in addition to MV-type animations (the MV-Type is a bit hidden behind right-click), the option to switch to manual layer control in mapping, improved plugin API as some of the big points and a lot of smaller improvements in the event commands and elsewhere.
So if you're deciding which to purchase, MZ wins in almost every case - the only negative to MZ is that several people have used obfuscation on their plugins (makes compatibility patches almost impossible) and more require payment for their plugins (which they are entitled to as they put the work in, but its something that should be mentioned)

posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
MV has a large available of plugins, MZ has effeskeer animations which
is way cooler (can have animation sheets.
so making your own animation also require (if you want it unique or modify it)
the use of a effeskeer software.
MZ has layered mapping, MV does not (but there is a plugin to do so as well).
as base of NWJS of MZ starts around 0.48.4 and PIXI 4.8.9 I believe, you can
update MV to have the same.
while MZ, MV share JS plugins, some functions are different or works different.
whatever you choose, you could take up the trial of both and see which one
works best for you, search plugins you want to use, and what engine (MV, MZ)
is available for your needs.
from there, you can decide probably better => use trials first, than decide.
I'm an MV user, and it works really good, but MV plugin command can get messy
where MZ is more organized in it.
so... its up to you which one to choose.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body: If you're starting from scratch, I would say there's almost no reason to choose MV over MZ now. The only exception I can think of would be if you know of a major MV plugin that you definitely need that's not compatible with MZ.

posts.author: Nirriti
posts.body: Just the layering alone makes it easy to answer MZ. However, some things out of the box are to be disabled via plugins, according to your own biases. For me early on, one of them were the HP/MP gauges. You cant do that natively. The capable people here (and elsewhere) are a blessing in that regard.

posts.author: Willibab
posts.body: I don't know anything about the technical stuff. I just felt the difference right away.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Use both. Make game in MV to take advantage of many a free plugin, use MZ to get the manual map layers and whatnot.
You can slap an MZ project file into your MV game folder and open your game just fine. You can do almost anything in MZ  but keep the MV code base. You can map in MZ, you can event in MZ (with a couple of small exceptions like the "Plugin Command" event command, which is a little different in MZ.) and take advantage of let's say the balloon preview and other QoL features MZ comes with.
You will have to skip using the particle animations of course, but imho 3d particles never looked good in a 2d game to begin with, but that's just my opinion.
In terms of the game performance, I've never noticed a difference.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
If you do that, you'll need to either be careful (there are at least 5 completely new features in the MZ engine off the top of my head) or use a plugin that makes MV forward-compatible with MZ data. But, yes, I'm pretty sure it's possible.
Other than the plugin commands being completely different, the following features in MZ won't work if your core code is MV:
Show Text –> Name
Get Location Info –> Designation by Character
Control Variables –> Game Data –> Last
Conditional Branch —> Button —> the second dropdown will always be treated as if you selected "pressed"
Move Picture —> Easing
I'm not sure if that list is exhaustive. You can use MV plugin commands in MZ just fine, but what you'll need to do is to find some event that already uses it and copy-paste from there. Either that, or use FOSSIL, which lets you embed MV commands into an MZ command.
There are some other non-event things that are new in MZ. Other than stuff on the System tabs, the only one I remember off the top of my head is the Attack Skill trait. And Effekseer animations of course.
